clips.title: The story
paras: In Red Cloud Mesa, A Humble Task sends young tauren to carry well water to Camp Narache. Greatmother Hawkwind asks for this service, a first lesson in humility and care for the tribe.

Greatmother Hawkwind has walked many trails, though age has slowed her across the plains. She tends to her duties beside the well on Red Cloud Mesa's southern edge. When young tauren with hopes of defending their people meet her, she turns their energy toward the needs of the community. Service gives them a chance to prove themselves through care for others.

You carry a filled pitcher northwest to Camp Narache and give it to Chief Hawkwind, the settlement's leader and Greatmother Hawkwind's son. Life across Mulgore's dry plains depends on shared labor and steady supplies of fresh water. By carrying a burden for an elder, you show respect for the people whose care holds the tribe together.

When you bring his mother's water to Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sees more than a chore completed. Tauren custom asks those who would champion their people across distant lands to begin with humility and a ready hand. Your quiet discipline catches the chief's eye, and he recommends you for the Rites of the Earthmother, spiritual tests that open the gates to Thunder Bluff.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: I have traveled many paths through life and these old legs lack the vigor they once had. I can still perform my duties to the tribe. Sometimes it just takes an old woman a little longer to do the task.
But you look like an eager adventurer. Let's put some of that youthful vitality to the test. Take a water pitcher from the well and bring it to my son, the Chief, in Camp Narache.
Remember that even the most humble task can gain the recognition of elders.

clips.title: Progress
paras: You look as though you have returned from the plains. Do you have any word from Greatmother Hawkwind?

clips.title: Completion
paras: You carried this pitcher back at the Greatmother's bidding, I see.
Your willingness to help others and provide for the traveler of Camp Narache leads me to believe you would make the tribe proud in Thunder Bluff someday.
